eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects high uncertainty in Paris's highest temperature on May 6, with 12°C (20.5%) and 13°C (21.0%) leading amid closely matched implied probabilities around 12–14°C, driven by Météo-France's latest short-range guidance forecasting maxima near 14°C under overcast skies and light showers, 3–4°C below seasonal norms of 18°C. ECMWF and GFS ensemble models show 2–3°C spreads due to northerly airflow advecting cool maritime air from the North Sea, persistent low-level clouds suppressing daytime heating, and variable precipitation timing. Thicker stratocumulus decks favor 11–13°C outcomes, while partial afternoon clearing could lift peaks to 15–16°C; monitor hourly updates from Météo-France and new ensemble runs overnight for shifts ahead of resolution at official Paris station observations.

eventMetadata.context_description: Divergent short-range forecast models from the China Meteorological Administration, ECMWF, and GFS are driving the tight race between 28°C or higher (41.5% implied probability) and 18°C or below (40.5%) for Chengdu's highest temperature on May 6, reflecting uncertainty in subtropical ridge persistence versus potential frontal cloud intrusion. After a cool, overcast May 3 high near 23°C limiting solar insolation, May 4 cleared to ~28°C and May 5 models converge on 30–31°C amid light winds and boundary layer heating; however, May 6 ensembles split with ECMWF/GFS averages ~26°C partly cloudy (AccuWeather 26°C) but CMA hinting showers could cap peaks below 20°C if moisture advection strengthens. Key differentiators include afternoon cloud cover and ridge breakdown risk; watch updated 12Z runs and Chengdu Shuangliu Airport observations for resolution. Early-May climatology averages 26°C, amplifying trader caution on extremes.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day by the Forecast for the Ninoy Aquino International Airport Station once information is finalized, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/ph/manila/RPLL.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve to "Yes" until all data for this date has been finalized.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is finalized for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: PAGASA's latest 5-day forecast for Port Area in Metro Manila projects a high of 35°C on May 6 amid persistent easterlies driving partly cloudy skies and isolated rainshowers, with 0-20% precipitation chance, fueling trader consensus on mid-30s outcomes at equal implied probabilities. This reflects May's climatological peak as the Philippines' hottest month, with historical Manila highs averaging 33-34°C but recent days consistently reaching 35°C under similar light winds and low humidity enhancing urban heat island effects. Differentiating factors include afternoon cloud cover variability—thicker layers could cap peaks at 33-34°C via reduced insolation, while clearer conditions and delayed sea breeze might boost to 36-37°C—though extremes remain unlikely given baseline trends and no tropical disturbances. Daily PAGASA updates expected to refine model consensus ahead of resolution.
